question: which river joins the estuary at Southwick

passages.title: Brent (river)
passages.text: The Brent flows south from the Carrow watershed and joins the estuary at Southwick.

passages.title: Southwick
passages.text: Southwick lies at the mouth of the Brent. Its quay handled grain until the 1950s.

passages.title: Estuaries of the eastern coast
passages.text: Three estuaries break the eastern coast: the Vell at Portsend, the Brent at Southwick, and the smaller Lyn at Eastfield.

question: how many bridges cross the Brent at Southwick

passages.title: Southwick
passages.text: Two bridges cross the Brent at Southwick, a road bridge of 1901 and a footbridge added in 1978.

passages.title: Brent (river)
passages.text: The Brent is bridged in four places along its lower course, twice at Southwick and twice above.

passages.title: Road bridges of 1901
passages.text: A programme of county road bridges was completed in 1901, including the Southwick crossing.

question: Which hills form the watershed between the Vell and the Brent?

passages.title: Carrow hills
passages.text: The Carrow hills form the watershed between the Vell, which flows east, and the Brent, which flows south.

passages.title: Vell (river)
passages.text: The Vell rises on the eastern flank of the Carrow hills.

passages.title: Brent (river)
passages.text: The Brent rises on the southern flank of the Carrow hills.

question: In which decade was the Portsend harbour wall completed?

passages.title: Portsend
passages.text: The harbour wall at Portsend was completed in 1829.

passages.title: Harbour walls of the eastern coast
passages.text: Portsend and Ashcombe harbour walls were both completed during the 1820s.

passages.title: Ashcombe
passages.text: Ashcombe is a small harbour north of Portsend, walled in 1826.

question: In which port were the charts of the estuary surveyed in the 1840s engraved?

passages.title: Survey of the Vell estuary
passages.text: The 1840s survey produced charts that were engraved in Portsend.

passages.title: Portsend
passages.text: Portsend is a port at the mouth of the Vell estuary.

passages.title: Hensley Ward
passages.text: Hensley Ward surveyed the Vell estuary between 1841 and 1849.

question: Which river does the town that gives its name to the Marl bridge stand on?

passages.title: Bridges of Marlbridge
passages.text: The Marl bridge is the oldest of the three crossings at Marlbridge.

passages.title: Marlbridge
passages.text: Marlbridge stands on the river Vell.

passages.title: Vell (river)
passages.text: The Vell flows east from the Carrow hills to Portsend.

question: What is the occupation of Alder Finch?

passages.title: Alder Finch
passages.text: Alder Finch was an engraver in Portsend who cut the plates for the 1849 estuary charts.

passages.title: Chart engraving
passages.text: Chart plates were cut by hand until photolithography displaced the trade.

passages.title: Portsend
passages.text: Portsend supported a small engraving trade serving the coastal chart market.

question: What is the occupation of Merrow Tate?

passages.title: Merrow Tate
passages.text: Merrow Tate served as harbourmaster at Southwick from 1888 until 1904.

passages.title: Southwick
passages.text: Southwick quay handled grain traffic under a succession of harbourmasters.

passages.title: Harbourmasters
passages.text: The harbourmaster held authority over berthing and pilotage within the harbour limits.
